extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance implementing 37 CFR 1.704 on when and how patent term adjustment (PTA) is reduced because an applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution. Enumerates specific applicant actions/inactions that trigger PTA reductions and how to compute the reduction periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant failure to engage in reasonable efforts (§ 1.704(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment of the term of a patent under §§ 1.703(a) through (e) shall be reduced by a period equal to the period of time during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution (processing or examination) of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C)(i). The Office may identify specific circumstances that constitute such a failure; reductions must equal the period of time the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts. See Supernus Pharm. v. Iancu (Fed. Cir.) for related interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply delays in excess of three months (§ 1.704(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is deemed to have failed to engage in reasonable efforts for the cumulative total of any periods of time in excess of three months taken to reply to any notice or action by the Office making any rejection, objection, argument, or other request, measuring the three-month period from the date the notice or action was mailed or given to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTA reduction is the number of days beginning the day after the date that is three months after mailing/transmission of the Office communication and ending on the date the reply was filed. The reply filing date is the date of actual receipt per § 1.6 (certificate-of-mailing/transmission dates under § 1.8 are not used). The three-month clock applies regardless of the reply period set in the Office action; weekend/holiday rules apply (next business day acceptance). A compliant reply under § 1.113(c), an appeal, or an RCE stops the three-month clock. Examples and case law (e.g., ArQule v. Kappos, Intra-Cellular Therapies v. Iancu) illustrate application, including treatment of final rejections and § 1.116 replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action at applicant's request (§ 1.704(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of action under § 1.103 at the applicant’s request constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the date a request for suspension under § 1.103 was filed and ending on the date of termination of the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of issuance under § 1.314 (§ 1.704(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Deferral of issuance of a patent under § 1.314 constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications with a notice of allowance mailed on or after July 16, 2020: reduction equals days from the date a request for deferral under § 1.314 was filed to the earlier of the date a request to terminate the deferral was filed or the date the patent was issued. Applicants can file a petition under § 1.182 to terminate deferral. For other applications, reduction runs from the date the deferral request was filed until the issue date of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment or late payment of issue fee (§ 1.704(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment of the application or late payment of the issue fee constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications with notice of allowance on/after July 16, 2020: reduction equals days beginning on the date of abandonment or the day after the issue fee was due and ending on the date a grantable petition to revive or accept late payment was filed. For other applications: reduction begins on abandonment or day after issue fee due and ends on the earlier of (1) date of mailing of decision reviving/accepting late payment or (2) the date that is four months after filing of the grantable petition (four-month cap measured from petition filing to limit reduction if Office doesn't act).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file petition to withdraw abandonment or revive within two months (§ 1.704(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment or to revive an application within two months from the date of mailing of a notice of abandonment constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date two months from mailing of the notice of abandonment and ending on the date a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment or to revive the application was filed. Applicants are encouraged to verify OPSG/PAIR records after petition grant to ensure correct recording of papers/dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of provisional to nonprovisional (§ 1.704(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of a provisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(b) to a nonprovisional application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) per 111(b)(5) constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the date the application was filed under 111(b) and ending on the date a request in compliance with § 1.53(c)(3) to convert the provisional to a nonprovisional was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment or paper filed <1 month before action/allowance (§ 1.704(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a preliminary amendment or other preliminary paper less than one month before the mailing of an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 that requires the mailing of a supplemental Office action or notice of allowance constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications with notice of allowance mailed on/after July 16, 2020: reduction runs from the day after the date that is eight months from filing (or national stage commencement) to the date the preliminary amendment/paper was filed. For other applications: reduction equals the lesser of (a) days from the day after the mailing date of the original Office action/notice of allowance to the mailing date of the supplemental Office action/notice of allowance, or (b) four months (four-month cap) — the cap limits reduction where the Office takes longer than four months to issue a supplemental action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of a reply having an omission (§ 1.704(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a reply having an omission (per § 1.135(c)) constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date the reply having an omission was filed and ending on the date that the reply or other paper correcting the omission was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of a supplemental reply or other paper after a reply (not expressly requested) (§ 1.704(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a supplemental reply or other paper, other than one expressly requested by the examiner, after a reply has been filed constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date the initial reply was filed and ending on the date the supplemental reply or other paper was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment after PTAB or Federal court decision filed <1 month before action/allowance (§ 1.704(c)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment or other paper after a decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (other than a decision with a new ground of rejection under § 41.50(b) or a § 41.50(c) statement), or after a Federal court decision, if filed less than one month before the mailing of an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 that requires a supplemental action, constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by number of days beginning on the day after the date of the PTAB or Federal court decision and ending on the date the amendment or other paper was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment under § 1.312 or other paper after notice of allowance (§ 1.704(c)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an amendment under § 1.312 or other paper, other than one expressly requested by the Office or an RCE in compliance with § 1.114, after a notice of allowance has been given or mailed constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 and ending on the date the amendment under § 1.312 or other paper was filed. Submission of a request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced PTA is not considered a failure under this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file appeal brief within three months (§ 1.704(c)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 within three months from the date on which a notice of appeal to the PTAB was filed (under 35 U.S.C. 134 and § 41.31) constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date three months from the notice of appeal filing and ending on the date an appeal brief in compliance with § 41.37 or a request for continued examination in compliance with § 1.114 was filed. Examples illustrate how the three-month clock and stopping events operate (e.g., when an applicant files an RCE or notice of appeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing RCE after notice of allowance (§ 1.704(c)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a request for continued examination (RCE) under 35 U.S.C. 132(b) after any notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151 has been mailed constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date of mailing of the notice of allowance and ending on the date the RCE was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to put application in condition for examination within eight months (§ 1.704(c)(13) and (f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to provide an application in condition for examination as defined in paragraph (f) within eight months from either the date the application was filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or the date of commencement of the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371(b) or (f) constitutes a failure to engage in reasonable efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTA shall be reduced by the number of days beginning on the day after the date that is eight months from filing/national stage commencement and ending on the date the application is in condition for examination. Paragraph (f) defines 'condition for examination' (see separate criterion) and explains that certain corrections made by the latest reply prior to the mailing of an action are treated as being in compliance as of that reply date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of continuing application prosecution (§ 1.704(c)(14))
rubrics_metrics.description: When further prosecution is via a continuing application, the period of adjustment set forth in § 1.703 shall not include any period that is prior to the actual filing date of the application that resulted in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents counting periods before the actual filing date of the continuing application as part of PTA for the patent that issues from the continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS-only submissions exception to failures (§ 1.704(d)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper containing only an information disclosure statement (IDS) in compliance with §§ 1.97 and 1.98, or an RCE that includes only an IDS, will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts under certain paragraphs if accompanied by a statement that each item of information in the IDS (i) was first cited in any communication from a patent office in a counterpart foreign/international application or from the Office and that communication was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to filing the IDS; or (ii) is a communication issued by a patent office in a counterpart foreign/international application or by the Office and was not received by any individual designated in § 1.56(c) more than thirty days prior to filing the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-day period is not extendable. The statement must be submitted on Office form PTO/SB/133 using document code PTA.IDS; otherwise the paper or RCE will be treated as not accompanied by the required statement unless an application for PTA establishing compliance is filed. No changes to statements on this form may be made; presenting the form constitutes a certification under § 11.18(b) that the text has not been altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA reinstatement request not a failure (§ 1.704(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission of a request under § 1.705(c) for reinstatement of reduced patent term adjustment will not be considered a failure to engage in reasonable efforts under paragraph (c)(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a § 1.705(c) reinstatement request itself will not trigger the § 1.704(c)(10) reduction rule for amendments after allowance; it is treated separately under the rules governing reconsideration and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for examination requirements (§ 1.704(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) is in condition for examination when it includes a specification (including at least one claim and an abstract (§ 1.72(b))), papers in compliance with § 1.52, drawings (if any) in compliance with § 1.84, any required English translation, Sequence Listing or Sequence Listing XML if applicable, an inventor's oath/declaration or application data sheet with the information in § 1.63(b), basic filing/search/examination fees, any certified copy required by § 1.57(a), and any required application size fee. International applications have analogous requirements per §§ 1.491 and 1.492.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application is considered to have papers/drawings/sequence listings in compliance for purposes of paragraph (f) on the filing date of the latest reply (if any) correcting those items that is prior to the date of mailing of either an action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151, whichever occurs first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and interpretive principle: reduction equals applicant's period of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.704 implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C), which provides that the period of PTA shall be reduced by the period during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts; the Office may prescribe regulations establishing circumstances that constitute such failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule does not require that the applicant's action/inaction caused or contributed to PTA; reductions apply regardless of causation. The regulations list exemplary circumstances and are not exhaustive; the Office may reduce adjustment based on other conduct that interferes with processing/examination under authority of 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C)(iii). The rules were amended (effective for certain applications/notices of allowance) to conform with Supernus Pharm., which clarified that reduction is the period from beginning to end of applicant's failure and cannot exceed that period.
